subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): scope subscription_limit blocks to the failing model

question: Should OpenClaw treat known-model OpenAI/Codex `subscription_limit` blocks as model-scoped for shared auth profiles while keeping unscoped or conflicting active blocks profile-wide?
rationale: The patch is a narrow implementation of an existing field, but it changes observable auth-provider routing for shared-profile users and upstream Codex exposes quota data by limit id/snapshot rather than a formal OpenClaw model-to-quota map.

options.title: Accept scoped blocks
options.body: Land after current-head validation if maintainers agree a subscription-limit block tied to one requested model should not suppress sibling models on the same profile.

options.title: Require stronger quota proof
options.body: Ask for explicit proof that the affected model ids map to separate Codex quota pools before accepting the behavior change.

options.title: Keep profile-wide blocks
options.body: Pause or close this PR if subscription-limit blocks must remain account/profile-wide regardless of requested model identity.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped blocks
recommendation.body: Land after current-head validation if maintainers agree a subscription-limit block tied to one requested model should not suppress sibling models on the same profile.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent auth-profile state/session history and is the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting compatibility choice.
